hints: Look at the overall shape and focus on the very high peaks followed by a sharp fall, as these mark a special change in period.
Notice that P and X are the tall peaks, while Q just after P is the very low trough, so identify which groups these must belong to.
Count forward from Q as Group 1 across the short period to assign R, S, T, U, V, W and X, remembering the small dips at S and V.
walkthrough:
**Spot the noble gases**

Think like a detective. First ionisation energy rises across a period and then falls sharply when a new shell starts. The highest points are the most stable atoms.

That means P and X with the very high values are noble gases (Group 18).

**Spot the start of a new period**

Right after P, the value crashes down to Q. That is because the next electron goes into a new shell, further out and more shielded, so it is very easy to remove.

So Q is an alkali metal (Group 1), the first element of the next period.

**Count across the period from Q to X**

From Q to X there are 8 elements, a typical p-block short period. Count them as Group 1 to Group 0:
$$Q(1), R(2), S(13), T(14), U(15), V(16), W(17), X(18)$$

**Check the two small dips for confirmation**

You can confirm this by the two small falls. R to S falls because S starts the p subshell, and U to V falls because V has a paired p electron with extra repulsion.

This pattern fits perfectly, so W must be Group 17, a halogen.

options.A: Incorrect. Q is not a noble gas. Q is the low trough immediately after the noble gas P, so it starts a new shell and is a Group 1 alkali metal. Students who choose this confuse the peak with the trough.
options.B: Incorrect. S is not a Group 2 element. R is Group 2, and S is the next element where ionisation energy drops because the p subshell begins, so S is Group 13. This traps students who count only the rise and ignore the subshell change.
options.C: Incorrect. V is not a Group 15 element. U is Group 15 with the half-filled p subshell ($p^3$) which is extra stable, and V is Group 16 ($p^4$) where spin-pair repulsion makes removal easier, so V is lower than U. This is the classic Group 15 to 16 dip.
options.D: Correct. Well done. Counting from Q as Group 1, W is the seventh element, one before the noble gas X. That makes W Group 17, a halogen. The steady rise from S to W, apart from the U to V dip, confirms this position.
